summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, pancreas and kidney transplants, end-stage renal disease, and chronic heart failure was admitted for shortness of breath and weakness. She presented with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and volume overload, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. Initial evaluation revealed pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and anemia. She underwent hemodialysis, which improved her respiratory status. Due to recurrent hypotension during dialysis, midodrine was initiated to support blood pressure and facilitate fluid removal. Warfarin was held in preparation for an upcoming peritoneal dialysis catheter placement. She received two units of packed red blood cells for anemia and was transitioned to extended care for recovery. Discharge planning included daily weight monitoring, continuation of immunosuppressive and cardiac medications, and readmission for anticoagulation management post-procedure.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
